_doc: Template for site.json (copy to site.json and fill in). site.json is git-ignored and holds every network-specific value.
_doc_site_name: Display name for this network, used in titles and reports.
_doc_own_domains: Domains you own (home.lan, example.com). Used to recognise your own names in DNS and certificates and by the push guard that blocks publishing them.
_doc_internal_cidr: Your whole internal address range (a CIDR such as a /16 or /8 private range). Used in Elasticsearch queries to select internal-to-internal traffic. It must contain every zone.
_doc_internal_prefixes: Address prefixes that count as internal (for example the first two octets plus a dot). Any IP starting with one is internal; others are internet. 'Discover from UniFi' fills them from your subnets. Wrong prefixes make internal traffic look external.
_doc_es_url: Elasticsearch (Security Onion) URL that netmon queries, for example https://sensor.example.lan:9200. Credentials are set under More > Configuration.
_doc_sensor_ip: IP of the Security Onion / network sensor. It sees all traffic, so it is treated as infrastructure and excluded from some detections.
_doc_self_ip: IP of the machine running netmon. Its own traffic (feeds, API calls) is expected and not reported.
_doc_self_host: Host name of the machine running netmon. Used to recognise its own events.
_doc_gateway_name: Display name of your router/firewall gateway.
_doc_gateway_dns_ip: The gateway's DNS address. DNS that bypasses it (clients using a public resolver directly) is flagged, and the fix text names this address.
_doc_unifi_console_ip: LAN IP of the UniFi console. Netmon reaches UniFi through the cloud API; this is for display and pivot links.
_doc_home_wan: Your home public IP. UniFi admin access from it, from internal addresses and from the VPN is expected; any other source is an alert.
_doc_vpn_prefixes: Address prefixes handed to VPN clients (for example '192.168.2.'). Admin access from them counts as expected.
_doc_honeypot_ips: IPs of decoy hosts. Any connection to one is suspicious because nothing legitimate uses it.
_doc_admin_workstations: Free text naming your admin machines. It is inserted into advice such as 'restrict SSH to <these> with a firewall rule'.
_doc_host_ips: Endpoint host name -> IP, so Elastic Agent hosts without a device IP are tied to the right address for risk scoring. Changes need a dashboard restart.
_doc_display_names: IP -> friendly name shown instead of the DHCP name or the bare address (IP -> kube-1).
_doc_crown_jewels: IP -> reason for your most important systems. They get the maximum impact (5) in risk scoring, so any weakness on them ranks highest. Changes need a dashboard restart.
_doc_game_ports: Port -> name of game servers you run (25565 -> minecraft). Used to label that traffic as expected rather than unknown.
_doc_vapid_contact: Contact (mailto:you@example.com) sent to browser push services with web-push notifications. Not shown to anyone else.
_doc_github_user: GitHub user that ship.sh pushes to, and that the push guard refuses to leak into other places. Only needed if you publish a fork.
_doc_github_repo: GitHub repository (user/name) that ship.sh pushes to. Only needed if you publish a fork.
_doc_image_repo: Container registry path for the dashboard image (ghcr.io/user/netmon-dashboard). Only needed if you publish images.
_doc_sensitive_terms: Words that must never appear in the public repository (your names, hosts, domains). repo_guard.py blocks a commit or push that contains one.
_doc_kibana_url: Kibana base URL. When set, the dashboard shows a magnifier button that opens the matching search in Kibana. Empty hides the buttons.
_doc_kibana_data_view: Kibana Discover data view id used by those links (default logs-*).
_doc_unifi_web_url: Base URL of the UniFi Network web app, for pivot links from a client or event straight into UniFi.
_doc_unifi_paths: Label -> page path under unifi_web_url for the UniFi pivot links (for example 'Flows' -> 'insights/flows').
